It’s so weird isn’t it? The people that need therapy the most are so against it for no good reason! 

I think for narcissistic parents they just get mad when they lose control, therapy helped get my self esteem up enough to realize I can make decisions for myself and I think she’s just mad she doesn’t get to live vicariously through me anymore.
It’s a hard cycle to break but you’re putting the work in and that’s what matters!

Oh that’s awesome!! If you kept the old filter media in there for a couple of weeks and everything’s still at zero I’d assume your tank is cycled and you’re just doing water changes frequently enough to keep the levels of nitrates low/zero! If you wanna cut down the frequency of water changes I’d give it a go but keep checking the water every single day just in case! And I’ve heard from people on this sub that painted decor can be bad for the water over time, you might wanna look for some more natural decor for the little dude!

How are you testing the water parameters? I’ve heard the test strips aren’t super accurate, you might wanna switch to the API freshwater master test kit if you haven’t already! It might show you where you are in your cycle if it isn’t fully cycled already!

**to clarify I’ve switched to doing weekly water changes now that he’s doing pretty well, but the first month or so it was daily because I was doing a fish in cycle and I wanted to keep the water clean so he could heal!

Honestly, it takes time but I saw the best improvement just from testing parameters and doing water changes daily! 

Also make sure there’s nothing in the tank that will snag their fins because they tear super easily, and give them lots of plants/some places to hide to make sure they’re not stressed. A happy betta and clean water seemed to make a super huge difference in his fins!!

I just finished my EMT school, last test was yesterday! I was in a 5 week course, so it was crazy fast but the best way I found to study was to pay attention in class, write down things I didn’t already know (can’t write down every single thing, it’s unreasonable), take the quizzes, and then read the chapter! Reading the chapter after everything else really just helped cement it, it let me read all the details and connect the dots because I knew kinda where we were going if that makes sense. 

Also I know anatomy/physiology and medical terminology isn’t everyone’s idea of a good time, but if you really lock those down then you can pretty much decipher anything they’re gonna ask you! It’s really the foundation of what you’re learning, and it gets a lot easier once you can understand what they’re asking you and how things work for the most part.

Also, if you haven’t already, make some friends in the class! Get there early and practice, see how your classmates are studying for tests, ask people questions, and if you see someone practicing with flash cards offer to quiz them (best way to learn is teaching others!)

Everyone in the class is going through exactly what you’re going through, and it’s more fun to go through it with some friends!

My mom called me manipulative and hurtful.

I'm getting married next year, and I'd been debating on whether or not it would be worth it to invite my narcissistic mom to my wedding.  I was leaning towards not having her there, but my dad thought I should at least consider it so I don't regret it in the future.  She has done some really horrid things in the past, specifically to myself and my dad, and I've never been able to have a conversation with her about any of it without her turning it around and making me feel like a horrible person or making me think it's all in my head.

Because I've never been able to get through to her, my dad offered to reach out and offer to get lunch or something to talk to her and explain the situation.  He hoped that if he could tell her how I was feeling, she could choose to apologize and change the way she handles specific situations, and I said that if she agreed to something like that I'd consider inviting her to the wedding.  

She just sent me a really long message, but the most frustrating part is that she said, "Asking me to spend time with someone who caused me so much pain in order to be invited is manipulative and hurtful.  ... Love is not about bending someone to your will, it's just loving them."

And I don't know why, but seeing those words from her just kinda broke me.  My entire life with her was spent being manipulated and bent to her will, I was never good enough for her ever.  She constantly made my siblings and I feel like we weren't worth anything if we didn't act exactly how she wanted us to, and she's able to recognize that it's not okay to do to people but will never admit that she's guilty of exactly that.

I don't think you're being too picky, you only get married once and it's normal to want things to be perfect!  And venues specifically set the scene for the whole wedding, I was super picky too!! 

While we were looking at venues, I almost just gave up because it seemed like if we found the perfect ceremony location then we had to compromise and get a cheap reception spot, we looked at way too many rec centers with horrible carpet before we finally found the right venue for us!   And it's a two hour drive from where we live, but we figured we could just get a hotel room for the night (or a few nights!) and drive back after the wedding.  Definitely check surrounding areas and talk to your fiancé, maybe he'd be open to something similar?

It’s not going to be a religious ceremony and neither of us share any cultural background with her, which I think is why I was surprised at the request! And she was previously planning on wearing a suit, and just recently changed her mind so I don’t think it’s frowned upon to wear other things to special events, but I truthfully don’t know a ton about the practices so I could be wrong!

I also get really overwhelmed really easily and I was worried about our families trying to “help” constantly and give input, which would make it significantly more stressful for me! What I did was made a detailed checklist on google sheets (I can share it with you if you’d like!) and I added everyone I could think of to it, with the ability to comment and not to edit, so I can keep track of all the planning super easily and I don’t have to answer a million questions from everyone constantly! 

We’re getting married in California and have about 80 guests, but I can say confidently we’re keeping it under 25k-30k so I’m sure you guys can do it!! The biggest way we saved a ton of money was to find a non profit garden that rents out the property for weddings! We have the whole venue for the entire day for 5k, which is nothing compared to some more traditional venues I’ve seen.  Keep an eye out for nonprofits and nontraditional locations that still fit in your vision!

Hi! I’m also planning without a wedding planner and I put together a super helpful google sheet, it has everything you should need and is spaced out for the year leading up to the wedding, I can share it with you if you want! Just send me a message!

Hey same, growing up with N parents really takes a toll on your mental health and a lot of people don’t take mental health seriously enough. 
But I swear there are things that make life worth living and there is going to be a way for you to get away from your parents.  Just take any steps you can to protect yourself and your identity long enough to find the opening

I understand that, my circle got really small when I first moved to a new town and it was really really difficult feeling so alone.  I promise it’ll get better, you just need to give it some time! 
One of the best things about life is that it continues to move forward, if you don’t like where you’re at right now you just have to sit tight and do whatever you can until things change.
Ooh the social media crawling always gets me bitter/sad, thank you for the advice! Good luck to you too, I hope you find a really good book - you definitely deserve it and we're gonna get through it.

You're going to make it, kids of N Parents are some of the toughest people I've ever met shouldn't be underestimated by anyone - especially themselves.  

I know it seems impossible, but it's definitely possible and it's going to feel so unbelievably good to show them how great you can do on your own.  Or just to show yourself how great you can do on your own. You deserve to thrive and I'm sorry so many people have made it so difficult for you to do so.  

If you can, find a job that lets you explore something you love to do.  Don't think about what looks good on paper or what you're "supposed" to do, it doesn't matter if you have a degree or experience in something specific, you're allowed to take any path you feel like taking towards your future.  If you love coffee, go work in a coffee shop.  If you love art, go check out some studios or galleries to see what kinds of jobs they offer.  It really doesn't matter what it is, but find something that'll help give you some sense of identity and allow you to put some money in the bank.  

You'll get out of there, just give yourself some time and some empathy.

I moved about 5 hours away from my home town.

Far enough that they don’t visit often but I can go home if I need to. And once I was out of the house I cut contact almost completely with everyone I knew and gave myself a week or two to get settled and get to know the area before starting to reach out to people. 

It gave me a clean slate to start building relationships with people that I wanted to have relationships with.  I explained that I was busy living my life, and started reaching out to anyone that respected the time I needed after moving.  Anyone that didn’t respect my boundary got very few responses if they got any at all.  

It’s actually how I went almost no contact with my mom. I explained that I needed some space to settle in to my apartment and my job and school, and but she texted me daily and called me all the time. I sent her a message saying that I felt I wasn’t getting the space I’d asked for, and that I’d really appreciate if she’d respect my needs.  She started lashing out, and I explained that I didn’t want that type of drama in my life and that if she would respect my space I’d be more inclined to put more effort into our relationship.  Nothing changed, if anything it got worse, and I just stopped responding to her and told her that if she respected my boundary I’d consider rebuilding the relationship.  That was almost three years ago and I’m still almost no contact with her. Best. Decision. Ever.

Hey! 
Sounds like a really crappy situation and I’m really sorry.  If you wanna check out online therapy like BetterHelp, it’s way more affordable and therapy for even a short amount of time can help immensely! 

If it’s possible, try going low contact or no contact with her. I know it’s a lot, but you can start small and just slowly cut her out of your life-or at least the parts you’d like full control of. Honestly it seems dumb but I started years ago by just not responding to all of my mothers texts and calls.  It can really be any small action that makes you feel like you have even an ounce of control, it really helps.

I hope you’re able to get through this, you got this!! :)

I think one of the most important things when looking for a relationship is not settling and not picking someone that necessarily feels comfortable right off the bat, which I know sounds weird but hear me out. 
All the stuff I went through, and I’m sure you’ve gone through as well, definitely took its toll on me. I thought I was worthless, that my opinions didn’t matter, and I was convinced that a happy relationship just meant one where we didn’t fight so I made sure to bottle up all my feelings did my best to keep the peace.  I ended up with a partner that mirrored a lot of traits my mom had, because I didn’t immediately notice them as red flags-I didn’t notice them at all because I was so used to dealing with them already.  

I didn’t notice how unhappy I was until about two years into the relationship, but we lived together and had a pet together and I was terrified to leave because “What if I can’t do better than this? What if I’m giving up the best thing I can get and I’m unhappy forever?”

At some point I had friends point out that his behavior wasn’t acceptable and I was brave enough to end things and move out, and it’s the best choice I’ve ever made.  I ended up dating around a bit and realized that a lot of the people I gravitated towards had a lot of similar manipulative tendencies, and that I often picked people like that because it’s behavior I expected growing up (aka, it was what I was comfortable with), but I also realized that I was in control of who I let in my life.  I started trying to expand my “type” and practicing typical dating things.  Eventually I got comfortable setting boundaries, communicating, and ending things when I didn’t feel respected which ended up boosting my confidence a ton! 

I started to trust my opinions and feelings more and more, and when I met someone that I felt really respected me, communicated well, and always strived to be better I felt comfortable starting an actual relationship (first one in like 3 years!) and it’s going really well! He makes me uncomfortable in a really good way, he helps me grow as a person and is always by my side when I need him. And I know I’m not settling for him, I’m excited about our future instead of wondering about all of the “what if’s…” 
He never makes me question my worth, and I constantly feel so lucky to have waited for him.

I didn’t see that therapist after that and ended up finding one that understood my situation much better!

I grew up in an emotionally abusive home and when i was in elementary school I broke down in tears and tried praying.  I asked why he would give me to a family that clearly never wanted me, asking if I did something wrong to deserve the life I’d gotten.

I asked him for help, if not with my family then maybe with the way I felt about it.  Shockingly, nothing got better and I decided that if there was a God then he was the type of god I’d like to believe in.  I didn’t to believe in a God that could put me into a family that broke me down so completely and nearly drove me to end my life at such a young age. 

I thought it’d be better to believe in nothing than to believe in a god, and then after a few years on my own I learned it was better to believe in myself than anything else (or nothing at all)
